raw: {"analysis": "Both responses provide structured plans addressing the key constraints: no refactoring, property-based testing, CI cost optimization, mock-ledger usage, and dual approval. MSX is more comprehensive and explicit: it includes a clear gate for verifying the safety net fails on injected violations, a detailed rollback plan, and a specific behavioral audit by Jane Smith. WJX has a slightly confusing gate numbering (G2, G4, G5, G6, G8) and lacks an explicit step to confirm the tests fail on artificial deviations, which is central to the request. MSX also better integrates the flaky currency check bypass into the harness design, while WJX only adds retry logic in CI. Overall, MSX offers a more actionable and complete plan with fewer ambiguities.", "verdict": "MSX"}
